source_caption:
𝐑𝐮𝐬𝐡𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞, 𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟖.⁣
⁣
Max Fischer (Jason Schwartzman) is a thirteen-year-old overachiever with a résumé that would make a Fortune 500 CEO blush. Clubs? He’s in all of them. Extracurriculars? He invented some. Pretending he’s the son of a neurosurgeon? Yep, that too. Max is insufferable, ridiculous, and completely irresistible. He’s the kind of kid who makes you cringe while rooting for him anyway. And let’s be honest, his crush on Miss Cross (Olivia Williams) is scandalously, hilariously inappropriate. This is the awkward teen love story we secretly love to watch. Then there’s Herman Blume (Bill Murray), a grown man flirting with existential crisis, midlife crisis, and an age-inappropriate crush all at once. On the first day of shooting, Wes Anderson whispered directions to Murray because he was so in awe and Murray, in classic form, not only deferred but helped haul equipment. When Disney shot down a helicopter scene costing $75,000, Murray literally gave Wes a blank check to make it happen. And he wanted the role so badly he would have done it for free. ⁣
⁣
Anderson’s genius is in how he makes you feel like you’ve wandered into a storybook world that’s slightly askew: symmetrical camera angles, perfectly timed music, and episodic storytelling that turns every scene into a chapter. The dancing scene at the end, with Max and Miss Cross swaying to the Faces’ “Ooh La La”, is heartbreak wrapped in melody, sweet and a little scandalous all at once. Rushmore (1998) is a straight-up comedy. But it’s also a love letter to the weird, the lonely and the ambitious. It’s about learning that all is considered fair when love is war. Even if you’re a ridiculous 13-year-old or a midlife crisis Bill Murray. This is cinema with heart, edge, and a little mischief.⁣
⁣
If you missed it the first time, give it another go. You’ll either fall in love with Max or laugh so hard you’ll never forget him. This is still Wes Anderson’s best movie.⁣
⁣
From book “𝟏𝟓𝟎 𝐅*𝐂𝐊𝐈𝐍𝐆𝐆𝐎𝐎𝐃𝐌𝐎𝐕𝐈𝐄𝐒”. Link in bio.⁣

source_details.title: Rushmore
source_details.synopsis: Rushmore is a 1998 American comedy film directed by Wes Anderson about a teenager named Max Fischer (Jason Schwartzman in his film debut), his friendship with rich industrialist Herman Blume (Bill Murray), and their shared affection for elementary school teacher Rosemary Cross (Olivia Williams). The film was co-written by Anderson and Owen Wilson. The soundtrack features multiple songs by bands associated with the British Invasion of the 1960s. Filming began in November 1997 around Houston, Texas, and lasted 50 days, until late January 1998. While the box office results were modest, the film had a positive reception among film critics.
